To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) the exchange of soft quantum fluctuations in high energy particle scattering can be described in a consistent way by the functional integration method of quantum field theory.

1) the scattering amplitude of particles interacting via exchange of an infinite number of soft quantum fields and a finite number of hard quanta is determined by the form factor of the interacting particles at large angles.

(1) the exchange of the hard quanta is responsible for a large contribution to the total scattering amplitude at high energies, and the contribution from the exchange of the soft quanta is relatively small.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the properties of the quarks and gluons, the elementary constituents of the proton.
the study of the properties of a new class of non-Abelian gauge theories with the gauge group $U(1)\times SU(N)$, where $N$ is a positive integer greater than one.
the study of the high-energy scattering of particles in the framework of the theory of the functional integration in quantum field theory.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the present work has provided a clear demonstration of the potential of the functional integral formalism to provide a unified and systematic treatment of the various problems in the field of hadronic interactions, and in particular to provide the necessary theoretical basis for the application of the method of the functional integral to the problem of the high energy scattering in the quantum field theory.

the present book, in the opinion of this reviewer, represents an excellent contribution to the field of high energy scattering and is strongly recommended for the graduate students, researchers, and teachers.

, while the method of functional integration in quantum field theory has been very successful in describing the scattering processes in quantum electrodynamics and in the theory of weak interactions, its application to the strong interactions is still in a very early stage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the method of functional integration in quantum field theory is the most convenient and effective method for the construction of the scattering amplitude of the interacting particles at large angles.
the elastic form factor is the basic object of high energy scattering theory, and the scattering amplitude is the form factor of the interacting particles.

we have shown that the exchange of soft quanta can be treated in a manner similar to the exchange of hard particles and that the exchange of hard quanta is a special case of the exchange of soft ones.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the exchange of the soft and the hard quanta in high energy scattering is the most important mechanism for the explanation of the experimental data.
, in the context of a particular model, the soft-hard duality is not a property of the S-matrix, but a property of the scattering amplitude.
we have developed a novel method for the construction of the high energy scattering amplitude of the particle which interacts through the exchange of the soft quanta and hard virtual particles.
